answers.assumption_check: Load-bearing: the launcher asks, the shim names, the launcher launches (Akien, outline 5.3.5.2.2, and the orchestrator's ruling), so the dispatcher must not compute the number itself. Not yet known: how the bash dispatcher asks a python module-level function (shim.name_instance, ticket d13859e2ae46); the build must decide (a small shim entry point, or python -c) and prove it. Also assumed: `cairn <device>.<n>` routing already launches instance n (bin/cairn header).
answers.builder_check: A Haiku builder cannot build this yet: the ask mechanism is undecided and the shim function (d13859e2ae46) and address helper (0f7a8cada1ca) are not on main. It is cast at TICKETME on purpose; the questions it needs answered are named in missing_check.
answers.children: none, because the dispatcher change is one flag and one proof; its dependencies are the sibling tickets d13859e2ae46 and 0f7a8cada1ca
answers.collision_check: Looked at superclaude (cairn/devices/cc/superclaude 262-296, ticket ae4d581be071, open-62a7f29771e6): the cc-specific bash next-free rule agrees in behaviour and stays as it is; moving it to ask the cc shim is a follow-on in out-bounds. Looked at d13859e2ae46 (the shim names; this asks it) and 0f7a8cada1ca (address lists instances): this depends on both and touches neither. No collision.
answers.falsifier_check: Clauses: (1) `cairn <device> start --new`, with <device>_0 live, asks the shim for the instance name and launches <device>.<n> for the number the shim returns, leaving instance 0 untouched | (2) when the shim refuses (an explicit name already live), the dispatcher exits non-zero with the shim's refusal on stderr and launches nothing. Horizon: red against HEAD (--new does not exist), green after, run on a scratch HOME so no live device is touched.
answers.gates_bound: proof gate (a hollow build must fail it) + durability gate (committed) + feeds-back-to-origin on failure (Laws 3 + 8).
